title: HW 17
subtitle: Stoichiometry (Mole Ratios, Grams to Grams) & Percent Yield

questions.q: Based on the balanced reaction below, 18 moles of H₂O would be produced from 12 moles of NH₃. 4 NH₃ + 5 O₂ → 4 NO + 6 H₂O
questions.note: 12 mol NH₃ × (6 mol H₂O / 4 mol NH₃) = 18 mol H₂O.

questions.q: Based on the balanced reaction below, 6 moles of H₂O would be produced from 8 moles of NH₃. 4 NH₃ + 5 O₂ → 4 NO + 6 H₂O
questions.note: 8 mol NH₃ × (6 mol H₂O / 4 mol NH₃) = 12 mol H₂O, not 6.

questions.q: In the following reaction, 10.0 moles of potassium would require how many moles of bromine? 2 K + Br₂ → 2 KBr
questions.note: 10.0 mol K × (1 mol Br₂ / 2 mol K) = 5.00 mol Br₂.

questions.q: For the reaction below, how many moles of nitrogen monoxide will form if we start with 2.0 moles of oxygen? 4 NH₃ + 5 O₂ → 4 NO + 6 H₂O
questions.note: 2.0 mol O₂ × (4 mol NO / 5 mol O₂) = 1.6 mol NO.

questions.q: Considering the balanced equation P₄ + 6 H₂ → 4 PH₃, finish the following sentence: Twelve (12) moles of H₂ _________.
questions.note: 12 mol H₂ × (4 mol PH₃ / 6 mol H₂) = 8 mol PH₃.

questions.q: Considering the balanced equation 2 Cu + O₂ → 2 CuO, finish the following sentence: Six (6) moles of Cu _________.
questions.note: 6 mol Cu × (2 mol CuO / 2 mol Cu) = 6 mol CuO. (It reacts with 3 mol O₂.)

questions.q: Balance the equation below and determine the number of moles of oxygen required to completely burn 5.00 moles of propane. C₃H₈ + O₂ → H₂O + CO₂
questions.note: C₃H₈ + 5 O₂ → 4 H₂O + 3 CO₂. 5.00 mol C₃H₈ × (5 mol O₂ / 1 mol C₃H₈) = 25.0 mol O₂.

questions.q: Flashback related to the question below! Methane, CH₄, reacts with oxygen following the pattern of a combustion reaction. Write and balance the reaction. What is the number in front of the H₂O after it is balanced without fractions?
Methane, CH₄, is found in natural gas. How many moles of oxygen are required to completely react with 4 moles of methane? You must first write and balance the combustion reaction.
questions.note: 4 mol CH₄ × (2 mol O₂ / 1 mol CH₄) = 8 mol O₂.

questions.q: According to the following reaction, what mass of silver nitrate would be required to react with 0.500 grams of potassium chloride? AgNO₃(aq) + KCl(aq) → AgCl(s) + KNO₃(aq)
questions.given: Molar mass of AgNO₃ = 169.87 g/mol · Molar mass of KCl = 74.55 g/mol
questions.note: 0.500 g KCl × (1 mol KCl / 74.55 g KCl) × (1 mol AgNO₃ / 1 mol KCl) × (169.87 g AgNO₃ / 1 mol AgNO₃) = 1.14 g.

questions.q: Consider the reaction: Na₂CO₃(aq) + 2 HCl(aq) → 2 NaCl(aq) + CO₂(g) + H₂O(l). If 24.43 g of sodium carbonate react completely, how many grams of NaCl will be produced? Report your answer with the correct number of significant figures.
questions.note: 24.43 g Na₂CO₃ × (1 mol / 105.99 g) × (2 mol NaCl / 1 mol Na₂CO₃) × (58.44 g NaCl / 1 mol NaCl) = 26.94 g.

questions.q: Consider the reaction: Na₂CO₃(aq) + 2 HCl(aq) → 2 NaCl(aq) + CO₂(g) + H₂O(l). If 17.41 g of sodium carbonate react completely, how many grams of NaCl will be produced? Report your answer with the correct number of significant figures.
questions.note: 17.41 g × (1 mol / 105.99 g) × (2 mol NaCl / 1 mol Na₂CO₃) × (58.44 g / 1 mol) = 19.20 g (keep the trailing zero: 4 sig figs).

questions.q: Consider the reaction: Na₂CO₃(aq) + 2 HCl(aq) → 2 NaCl(aq) + CO₂(g) + H₂O(l). If 32.97 g of sodium carbonate react completely, how many grams of HCl will be required? Report your answer to the correct number of significant figures.
questions.note: 32.97 g × (1 mol / 105.99 g) × (2 mol HCl / 1 mol Na₂CO₃) × (36.46 g HCl / 1 mol HCl) = 22.68 g.

questions.q: Consider the reaction below: 3 Ca(NO₃)₂(aq) + 2 Na₃PO₄(aq) → Ca₃(PO₄)₂(s) + 6 NaNO₃(aq). How many grams of Ca₃(PO₄)₂ will be produced if 6.85 g of Na₃PO₄ react completely?
questions.given: Molar mass of Na₃PO₄ is 163.94 g/mol · molar mass of Ca₃(PO₄)₂ is 310.18 g/mol · enter your answer in decimal form rounded to the correct number of significant digits.
questions.note: 6.85 g × (1 mol Na₃PO₄ / 163.94 g) × (1 mol Ca₃(PO₄)₂ / 2 mol Na₃PO₄) × (310.18 g / 1 mol) = 6.48 g.

questions.q: Consider the balanced reaction below: 3 Ca(NO₃)₂(aq) + 2 Na₃PO₄(aq) → Ca₃(PO₄)₂(s) + 6 NaNO₃(aq). How many grams of Ca(NO₃)₂ will be used completely in the reaction if 1.65 g of Na₃PO₄ react completely?
questions.given: Molar mass of Na₃PO₄ is 163.94 g/mol · molar mass of Ca(NO₃)₂ is 164.09 g/mol · enter your answer in decimal form rounded to the correct number of significant digits.
questions.note: 1.65 g × (1 mol Na₃PO₄ / 163.94 g) × (3 mol Ca(NO₃)₂ / 2 mol Na₃PO₄) × (164.09 g / 1 mol) = 2.48 g.

In the chemical reaction below, the theoretical yield of CCl₂F₂ was calculated to be 203.13 grams. If the percent yield in the reaction was 74.3%, how many grams of CCl₂F₂ were obtained? AsF₃ + CCl₄ → AsCl₃ + CCl₂F₂
questions.given: Do not round intermediate results. Type the answer with the correct number of significant figures. Do not include the unit.

questions.q: Methanol can react in the presence of sulfuric acid to produce dimethyl ether. Calculate the percent yield for this reaction, run in a laboratory starting with 50 grams of methanol and producing 26 grams of dimethyl ether. 2 CH₃OH → (CH₃)₂O + H₂O
questions.given: Make sure you calculate the theoretical yield of dimethyl ether first! Molar mass of CH₃OH = 32.04 g/mol · molar mass of (CH₃)₂O = 46.09 g/mol
questions.note: Theoretical: 50 g × (1 mol / 32.04 g) × (1 mol (CH₃)₂O / 2 mol CH₃OH) × (46.09 g / 1 mol) = 35.96 g. 26 ÷ 35.96 × 100 = 72 %.

questions.q: Calculate the percent yield of CCl₂F₂: 3.95 g of AsF₃ reacted completely with excess CCl₄. In a lab, a student actually obtained 2.1 g of CCl₂F₂. 2 AsF₃ + 3 CCl₄ → 2 AsCl₃ + 3 CCl₂F₂
questions.tag: Answer worked out, not from eLearn
questions.note: Theoretical: 3.95 g AsF₃ × (1 mol / 131.92 g) × (3 mol CCl₂F₂ / 2 mol AsF₃) × (120.91 g / 1 mol) = 5.43 g. 2.1 ÷ 5.43 × 100 = 38.7 % → 39 % (2 sig figs). Your PDF cut off before this question's answer, so it is calculated here with the class molar masses.
